Storm reviews: the strongest lows, one at a time

← Back to the archive
ERA5 proxy, not direct observation. Every storm here was found in ERA5 reanalysis by the project's pipeline A tracker, and every chart is drawn from ERA5 fields (0.25°, 6-hourly). 17 of the 30 are before the 2004–05 season, where no archive record exists; the other 13 are since then, and are still read here from ERA5. ERA5 smooths the very strongest winds and pressure minima, so real peaks may be stronger. These are case studies, not a trend: nothing here says whether such storms are becoming more or less common.

Hours at HF strength is the number of 6-hourly fixes with a gust index of at least 71.7 kt times six, counted from the first to the last such fix. Peak gust index is the highest ERA5 gust within 800 km over the ocean, one number per fix. Click a storm name to jump to its review.

Show:

Atlantic #1North Atlantic, 15 December 1986

Rank 1 by lowest ERA5 central pressure in the North Atlantic. ERA5 proxy, pipeline A track 72089.
912.3lowest pressure (hPa)
53fastest 24 h fall (hPa)
102peak gust index (kt)
48hours at HF strength
In plain words

ERA5 puts its lowest pressure at 912.3 hPa on 15 Dec 1986 0000Z, near 59.8°N 34.8°W. Its fastest 24 h fall was 53 hPa, ending 14 Dec 1986 1800Z at about 57°N (the bomb threshold there is 23 hPa, so it qualifies as a bomb by that yardstick). It first reached hurricane-force-equivalent gusts (index at least 71.7 kt) on 14 Dec 1986 1200Z near 58.5°N 35.0°W, was at that strength in 8 of its 6-hourly fixes (about 48 h from first to last), and peaked at a gust index of 102 kt on 15 Dec 1986 0600Z. The gust swath maximum anywhere in the window, land included, is 102 kt.

Not direct observation. This storm is before the 2004–05 season. No archive record covers it, so every number and map here is ERA5 reanalysis. The gust index also runs high before 2001 (ERA5 gust drifts upward at fixed storm depth), so read its level with caution; central pressure is the better yardstick. No trend is drawn from it.

How it developed
Weather maps every 12 hours

Its fastest 24 h fall was 45 hPa, ending 22 Feb 1998 0600Z at about 44°N (the bomb threshold there is 19 hPa, so it qualifies as a bomb by that yardstick). It first reached hurricane-force-equivalent gusts (index at least 71.7 kt) on 21 Feb 1998 0600Z near 38.5°N 153.5°E, was at that strength in 8 of its 6-hourly fixes (about 54 h from first to last), and peaked at a gust index of 80 kt on 23 Feb 1998 0000Z. The gust swath maximum anywhere in the window, land included, is 83 kt.

Not direct observation. This storm is before the 2004–05 season. No archive record covers it, so every number and map here is ERA5 reanalysis. Method

How the storms were chosen and drawn

The storms are those with the lowest ERA5 central pressure in each basin among the 1979–2025 tracks of pipeline A (the research tracker, research/era5/hf_history), taken in order of pressure from the lowest. Tropical-cyclone-flagged tracks are left out (three Pacific tracks, among them 30 Oct 1989 and 3 Oct 1981, which would otherwise rank second and third), and one Pacific storm from the 2024–25 season is left out because the weather-map fields used here end in January 2023. The rank shown is the rank among all tracks, so some numbers are missing. Ranking is by pressure alone, so the list is not a list of the strongest winds.

Central pressure, position and gust index come from the 6-hourly pipeline A fixes. The gust index is the highest ERA5 10 m gust over ocean within 800 km of the low. The weather maps use WeatherBench2 ERA5 at 0.25°, 6-hourly (sea-level pressure, 500 hPa geopotential height, 250 hPa wind speed), re-centred on the storm at each map time. The swath uses ERA5 hourly instantaneous gusts every 3 h over the 72 h window. The 24 h fall is the change in central pressure over the previous 24 h at each 6-hourly fix; the bomb line scales 24 hPa per 24 h at 60°N by sin(latitude)/sin(60°). OPC warns on sustained winds; the gust index is a proxy for that, not the same thing.

Read with care. ERA5 proxy throughout, never validated for storms before the archive begins. Before 2001 the gust index drifts upward at fixed storm depth, so gust numbers for the 1980s and 1990s storms are less reliable than their pressures. Not independently re-checked: how closely these ERA5 pressures match the observed minima of the named storms.

Seasons run 1 June to 31 May. Fields: WeatherBench2 ERA5 and ARCO-ERA5 (Google Cloud public data). Back to the archive
